title: no-halt-agent hardening — races + test hygiene + agent orphan-GC

decisions_S64c835_1.title: Reproduced both pre-existing races before fixing (AC-S64c835-1-1/2)
decisions_S64c835_1.detail: go test -race ./internal/tab/claudetui/ -count=1 on the base commit reproduced 29 identical DATA RACE reports, all charmbracelet/x/vt (*Emulator).Close() writing its internal `closed` bool (emulator.go:265) racing (*Emulator).Read() reading it (emulator.go:252), reached via daemon.go's spawnWithArgs drainer goroutine (Read, daemon.go:820) vs teardown (Close, daemon.go:1413). Separately reproduced roleCoordinator.OnUnsubscribe: a write to rc.subs at role.go:155 (under rc.mu) racing an UNGUARDED read of len(rc.subs) at role.go:172 in a DIFFERENT concurrent OnUnsubscribe call — the debug-log line ran len(rc.subs) *after* rc.mu.Unlock().

decisions_S64c835_1.title: roleCoordinator fix: capture counts under the lock (AC-S64c835-1-2)
decisions_S64c835_1.detail: OnSubscribe and OnUnsubscribe both had the same bug shape: len(rc.subs) read for a slog.Debug call *after* rc.mu.Unlock(). Fixed both by capturing the count into a local variable while still holding rc.mu, then using that local in the (now-unlocked) log call. No behavior change, no new locking, no deadlock risk — pure hoist of a read to inside an already-held critical section. Added TestRoleCoordinatorConcurrentSubscribeUnsubscribe (32 workers x 50 rounds of Subscribe/TakeActive/Unsubscribe) as a regression test; verified it fails under -race with role.go reverted to its old form and passes with the fix.

decisions_S64c835_1.title: Emulator fix: attempted palmux2-side mutex first, proved it cannot work
decisions_S64c835_1.detail: First attempt: added a closeMu to internal/tab/claudetui/Emulator, held by Read() for its entire (potentially indefinite) call, with Close() using closeMu.TryLock() to avoid deadlocking against a blocked Read(). This still raced under -race even with an increasingly generous bounded retry (tried 0ms and 200ms budgets with runtime.Gosched() spin). Root cause understood after the second failure: go test -race's race detection is based purely on the presence/absence of a happens-before edge (an actual synchronization primitive shared between the two accesses), not on wall-clock proximity — waiting longer before Close()'s unsynchronized fallback call does not create that edge, so the race is reported regardless of how much real time separates the two accesses. A mutex that Read() holds for its full (unboundedly long) call cannot be shared with Close() without either deadlocking (Close() waiting on a lock a permanently-blocked Read() holds) or leaving this exact un-closeable gap. Concluded this is provably unsolvable via palmux2-side wrapping alone, given io.PipeReader (which the underlying `closed` bool guards) offers no deadline/cancel support and vt.Emulator's pr/pw fields are unexported.

decisions_S64c835_1.title: Emulator fix: root-cause patch via local module replace (AC-S64c835-1-1)
decisions_S64c835_1.detail: Since the actual bug is charmbracelet/x/vt's Emulator.closed being a plain (unsynchronized) bool touched by both Close() and Read()/Write() from different goroutines, and SafeEmulator (which claims thread-safety) does not fix this (Close isn't overridden at all; Read explicitly bypasses SafeEmulator's own mutex) — patched a local copy of the exact same module version at third_party/charmbracelet-x-vt-racefix, changing only Emulator.closed from `bool` to `atomic.Bool` (3 call sites: 2 Load, 1 CompareAndSwap replacing the old read-then-write). Wired in via a `replace` directive in go.mod (scoped, documented, minimal — no other files touched, test files stripped from the copy). io.PipeReader.Read/io.PipeWriter.CloseWithError (what Close ultimately calls) are already safe for concurrent use per io.Pipe's own design, so this is the complete, root-cause fix — no additional palmux2-side locking needed. Simplified internal/tab/claudetui/Emulator.Close()/Read() back to plain pass-throughs. This departs from the story's 'serialize on palmux2's side' framing, but that framing did not anticipate that Read() can block indefinitely while Close() must interrupt it — a combination proven unsolvable with pure caller-side synchronization; the decisions above document why. Backlog item 'charmbracelet/x/vt Emulator.Close vs Read' should be closed by dropping the replace directive once upstream ships an equivalent fix.

decisions_S64c835_1.title: Regression tests proven to catch both original bugs
decisions_S64c835_1.detail: Added TestEmulatorCloseRacesReadAndFeed (20 iterations, mirrors daemon.go's drainer/readLoop/teardown goroutine triple) and TestRoleCoordinatorConcurrentSubscribeUnsubscribe. Confirmed each fails under -race when its corresponding fix is reverted in isolation (git stash on role.go alone; git stash on go.mod alone to restore the unpatched vt module) and passes with the fix restored. Also incidentally caught a related, previously-undocumented Feed()-vs-Close() race on the same `closed` field (SafeEmulator.Write takes se.mu but Close bypasses it entirely) — fixed by the same atomic.Bool patch.

decisions_S64c835_1.title: Final verification (AC-S64c835-1-1/2/3)
decisions_S64c835_1.detail: go build ./... clean. go vet ./... clean. go test ./internal/tab/claudetui/ (non-race) PASS. go test -race ./internal/tab/claudetui/ -count=3 -v: 300/300 PASS, 0 DATA RACE reports. Repeated -count=3 -race run concurrently with `stress-ng --cpu 8` for ~110s (simulating a loaded CPU per the AC wording): still 0 races. PALMUX_SURVIVAL_SMOKE=1 go test ./internal/tab/claudetui/ -run TestParallelInstances -count=1: PASS, no regression. No leaked fake_claude/ptyhost processes after any run (verified via pgrep).

story_S64c835_3_implementation_notes.title: claude-agent orphan-GC (claudetui parity)
story_S64c835_3_implementation_notes.summary: Mirrors internal/tab/claudetui's S3f2658-3 GCOrphans (discover.go) into internal/tab/claudeagent, piggybacking the SAME store 10s scanPorts tick (no new loop). Closes the backlog gap left open at S862203-3's done time: a branch/repo closed while palmux2 was DOWN previously left its agent pipe-mode ptyhost running forever until the branch happened to be reopened.
changes: internal/tab/claudeagent/discover.go: scanAgentRunDir now takes a skipLive(repoID,branchID,tabID) param (mirrors claudetui's scanRunDir) — referenced entries are excluded BEFORE any liveness dial, never touched. DiscoverAndRestore passes nil (unchanged behavior). New Manager.GCOrphans(ctx, isLive) scans + SHUTDOWNs every unreferenced LIVE ptyhost via a new sendAgentOrphanShutdown (raw dial + PipeClient.Shutdown, bypasses any live Agent/Client). New reapAgentContainerClaude mirrors claudetui's reapContainerClaude for in-container claude reap on GC-triggered SHUTDOWN (S52fc2c-4/S3f2658-4 parity), adapted to claudeagent's RuntimeResolver (runtime.ExecCommander instead of runtime.PTYCommander) via the same runtime.ContainerProcessKiller optional-capability type assertion.

internal/store/sync_worktree.go: new AgentOrphanGC interface + Store.SetAgentOrphanGC + Store.gcAgentOrphans, wired into the SAME runPortScan 10s tick right after gcTuiOrphans. gcAgentOrphans reuses Store.isTuiTabLive as its isLive predicate — deliberately NOT a fresh isAgentTabLive: isTuiTabLive is not actually claude-tui-specific, it's a plain store.Tab(repoID,branchID,tabID) existence lookup, and a Claude AGENT tab's id ("claude:claude", "claude:claude-2", ...) lives in the exact same per-branch TabSet as every other tab type (claude-tui uses the same ids too — they're mutually exclusive per-tab, distinguished by Tab.Type "claude" vs "claude-tui", but GCOrphans only ever needs existence-by-id).
internal/store/store.go: new agentGC AgentOrphanGC field alongside the existing tuiGC field.

cmd/palmux/main.go: st.SetAgentOrphanGC(agentManager) wired right after the existing DiscoverAndRestore call for claudeagent, before st.Run(ctx) starts the scan loop (same ordering discipline as claudetui's wiring).

internal/tab/claudeagent/discover_test.go (new): TestGCOrphans_ShutsDownUnreferenced_LeavesReferenced, TestGCOrphans_IDContainingDoubleUnderscore_SurvivesGC, TestGCOrphans_NilIsLive_IsNoOp — near-verbatim mirrors of claudetui/discover_test.go's equivalent tests, adapted to pipe-mode ptyhosts (ptyhost.ModePipe) and the fake_ndjson emitter (internal/ptyhost/testdata/fake_ndjson.go) claudeagent's own pipe-mode tests already use — real processes, not real claude.

internal/store/agent_orphan_gc_test.go (new): TestGCAgentOrphans_NoopWithoutGC, TestGCAgentOrphans_CallsWiredGC, TestGCAgentOrphans_TuiAndAgentGC_BothWired — mirrors tui_orphan_gc_test.go, plus a joint test proving both reapers fire independently on the same tick (the actual production wiring shape).
story_S64c835_3_implementation_notes.identity_discipline: Same S3f2658-3 discipline: identity is read from the ptyhost status file's EXPLICIT RepoID/BranchID/TabID fields (already written by ptyhost.Config since S862203-3's pipe-mode support), never by re-splitting the "__"-joined Seed string. TestGCOrphans_IDContainingDoubleUnderscore_SurvivesGC proves a repoID containing the literal substring "__" (e.g. "my__tool--ab12") round-trips exactly and is never misattributed/killed across several GC ticks.
story_S64c835_3_implementation_notes.gc_safety: skipLive-before-dial: scanAgentRunDir consults skipLive (== isLive, threaded through from GCOrphans) immediately after resolving identity from the status file and BEFORE the pidAlive check, the socket dial, or the HELLO probe. A referenced entry is left completely untouched — never counted as live, never counted as cleaned, never dialed. This matters beyond efficiency: a pipe-mode ptyhost socket only tolerates ONE active connection (ptyhost.Server.replaceConn evicts whichever connection was previously active the instant a new one arrives), so a liveness-probe dial against an entry this same process already has a live Agent/Client attached to would silently evict that connection out from under it.
story_S64c835_3_implementation_notes.backlog_closed: This closes the gap explicitly flagged in cb2a60e (chore(S862203-3): mark story done + backlog (claudeagent orphan-GC gap)) and in discover.go's own pre-S64c835-3 doc comment ("Unlike claudetui, there is no orphan-GC half here yet").
story_S64c835_3_implementation_notes.worktree_state_note: The isolated worktree this story was implemented in was initially branched from an older `main` commit that PREDATED the S64c835 plan commit and the entire S862203 (pipe-mode ptyhost) merge — i.e. internal/tab/claudeagent/discover.go, launch.go, ptyclient.go, offsetstore.go etc. did not exist in the worktree at task start. Fast-forwarded (`git merge --ff-only autopilot/main/S64c835`) onto the branch this story was actually meant to build on before starting any work; the worktree had zero divergent commits so this was a clean, non-destructive fast-forward.

verification.go_test: pass: go test ./internal/tab/claudeagent/... ./internal/store/... ./cmd/... (non-race, real fake_ndjson processes for the 3 new GCOrphans tests, ~1s each, no PALMUX_SURVIVAL_SMOKE gate needed — same convention as this package's other fakeNDJSONBin-based tests, which are hermetic and fast, unlike the heavier real-binary/real-detached-process survival_gate_test.go tests)
